title: Give a checked exception the four standard constructors

blocks.text: `Exception` offers four public constructors, and a custom exception usually mirrors them. Write the checked `ReportGenerationException` with all four, each handing its arguments to the matching superclass constructor:
Each form must behave exactly as the same form of `Exception` does, including what it leaves unset. `initCause` is a good way to find out whether a cause was set at all.

cases.says: The (message, cause) constructor keeps both, and the cause is the very object passed in.
The no-argument constructor leaves the message and the cause null, as Exception() does.
The cause-only constructor's message is cause.toString(), class name included.
The message-only constructor leaves the cause unset, so initCause can still set it once.

concepts: initCause sets a missing cause once, and cannot replace a cause a constructor already set.
The four standard constructors take nothing, a message, a message and a cause, or a cause alone.
